web_evidence.title: Herzog Visits Chicago
web_evidence.note: Authorized prepublication interior excerpt sustains external third-person scene narration while distinguishing Herzog's first-person thoughts and speech as locally embedded consciousness.

web_evidence.title: Herzog Reader's Guide
web_evidence.note: The publisher's guide explicitly says that despite extensive epistolary material and the narrator's intimacy with Herzog, the novel is not a first-person narrative.

web_evidence.title: Saul Bellow's Creation of Ambiguity and Deception in Herzog and The Dean's December
web_evidence.note: University thesis analysis identifies a nonpersonal third-person narrator who mediates Herzog's perceptions and explains that free indirect discourse blurs the distance between narrator and character.

web_evidence.title: Saul Bellow's Vision Beyond Absurdity: Jewishness in Herzog
web_evidence.note: Scholarly analysis describes movement from third person to first person and back during stream-of-consciousness remembrance; this documents surface viewpoint shifts but does not establish an autonomous participating base narrator.

person_note: The controlling voice is a nonparticipating, intimate third-person narrator centered on Moses Herzog. The event passages q01303, q01310, q01321, and q01330 independently show sustained third-person scene narration. First-person material is Herzog's speech, stream of consciousness, recollection, or extensive unsent correspondence: q01308 is situated in his letter to the Monsignor, and q01322 is explicitly introduced as his thinking. Some scholarship calls the resulting pronominal movement an alternation between first- and third-person viewpoints, but the publisher guide explicitly distinguishes the epistolary and intimate material from the novel's narrative person, while the authorized excerpt and narratological thesis show the third-person voice retaining scene-level control. The remaining ambiguity concerns the unusually blurred boundary created by free indirect discourse, not the participation of the base narrator.
